summary: Feed s182_triple to 10Gbps APM is degraded: 53.3% one-way TCP sessions breaks bidirectional transaction correlation, 15.34 Gbps microbursts overload the tool port (153% capacity), and 9.1% duplicates waste capacity and skew APM metrics.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of flows to the same APM tool port - likely asymmetric routing with separate TAP/SPAN inputs or per-direction load-balancing without symmetric hashing, so only one side of 270/507 sessions reaches the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) to correlate request/response and measure latency; 53.3% one-way sessions means broken transaction traces, inaccurate response times, and missed application performance detections.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM port using symmetric 5-tuple hashing on the packet broker to restore full bidirectional visibility.

findings.root_cause: Microburst of 15.34 Gbps in 1ms exceeds the APM's 10 Gbps port capacity (153% load) - packet broker is forwarding too much aggregate traffic to a single tool port without load-balancing or filtering.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM port overrun causes buffer drops and missed packets during bursts, leading to incomplete transactions and gaps in APM coverage despite no drops detected in capture window yet.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ APM ports with symmetric load-balancing to keep per-port rate <80% of 10Gbps and preserve bidirectional flow integrity while handling bursts.

findings.root_cause: 9.1% duplicate packets (570/6265) indicates same traffic arriving via multiple TAP/SPAN feeds aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker, or SPAN duplicate forwarding.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM wastes CPU/storage processing duplicates, inflates transaction counts and latency calculations, and duplicates exacerbate the 15.34 Gbps overload on the 10Gbps port.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short window before delivery to the APM, cutting ~9% load and correcting metrics.
